title: End of World War II
description: Japan's formal surrender ended World War II, following Germany's surrender in May. The war reshaped the global order and set the stage for the Cold War.

sources.dataset: End of World War II in Europe

title: Founding of the United Nations
description: Fifty-one countries founded the United Nations in the aftermath of World War II, establishing a global forum for diplomacy, peacekeeping, and international law.

title: Bretton Woods institutions come into force
description: The IMF and the World Bank formally came into existence when 29 countries ratified the Bretton Woods agreements, creating the post-war financial architecture of fixed exchange rates and development lending.

title: Philippine independence from the United States
description: The United States granted full independence to the Philippines under the Treaty of Manila, one of the first post-war decolonizations and a template for the wave that followed.

title: Truman Doctrine
description: President Truman pledged US support to Greece and Turkey against communist pressure, committing the United States to containment and marking an opening move of the Cold War.

title: Independence and Partition of India
description: British India gained independence and was partitioned into India and Pakistan, triggering one of the largest mass migrations in history amid widespread violence.

title: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade signed
description: Twenty-three countries signed the GATT in Geneva, launching the rounds of tariff reduction that governed world trade until the WTO replaced the agreement in 1995.

sources.dataset: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade

title: Communist coup in Czechoslovakia
description: The Communist Party seized full control of Czechoslovakia, completing the Soviet consolidation of Eastern Europe and hardening the division of the continent.

title: Marshall Plan
description: The United States committed some $13 billion in aid to rebuild Western European economies, tying reconstruction to trade liberalisation and Western political alignment.

title: Founding of the State of Israel
description: Israel declared independence following the UN partition plan for Palestine, immediately triggering the first Arab-Israeli war.

title: First Arab–Israeli War
description: Neighbouring Arab states invaded the newly declared State of Israel. The armistices that ended the fighting set borders that lasted until 1967 and displaced most of the Palestinian Arab population.

title: Berlin Blockade and Airlift
description: The Soviet Union cut off land access to West Berlin; Western allies supplied the city by air for eleven months, in the first direct confrontation of the Cold War.

title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
description: The UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the first global statement of rights that all people are entitled to and the basis of later human-rights treaties.

title: Founding of NATO
description: Twelve North American and European countries formed the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a collective-defense alliance that became central to Cold War geopolitics.

title: Founding of the People's Republic of China
description: Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China after the Communist Party's victory in the Chinese Civil War, sending the Nationalist government to Taiwan.

sources.dataset: Proclamation of the People's Republic of China

title: Republic of China government retreats to Taiwan
description: After defeat in the Chinese Civil War, the Nationalist government moved to Taipei, creating the divided political status across the Taiwan Strait that persists today.

title: Dutch recognition of Indonesian independence
description: The Netherlands transferred sovereignty to Indonesia after a four-year war, four years after Sukarno's 1945 declaration of independence.

title: Korean War
description: North Korea's invasion of South Korea drew in a UN-led coalition and later China, ending in an armistice that left the peninsula divided along the 38th parallel.

title: Founding of the Warsaw Pact
description: The Soviet Union and seven Eastern European states signed a mutual-defence treaty in response to West Germany's admission to NATO, formalising the military division of Europe.

title: Vietnam War
description: A prolonged conflict between communist North Vietnam and the US-backed South ended in North Vietnamese victory and the reunification of Vietnam under communist rule.

title: Hungarian Revolution
description: A nationwide uprising against Soviet-imposed rule was crushed by Soviet troops, ending hopes of reform within the Eastern Bloc for a generation.

title: Suez Crisis
description: Egypt's nationalization of the Suez Canal triggered an invasion by Britain, France, and Israel, which ultimately withdrew under US and Soviet pressure — a marker of Britain and France's declining global power.

title: Ghana becomes independent
description: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence from European rule, and Kwame Nkrumah's government became a rallying point for pan-Africanism.

title: Treaty of Rome / founding of the EEC
description: Six European countries signed the Treaty of Rome, establishing the European Economic Community — the direct institutional ancestor of today's European Union.

title: Cuban Revolution
description: Fidel Castro's forces overthrew the Batista government, producing the first communist state in the Western Hemisphere and a permanent flashpoint in US–Soviet relations.

title: "Year of Africa": mass African decolonization
description: Seventeen African countries gained independence from colonial rule in a single year, marking the peak of the continent's decolonization wave.

title: Congo Crisis
description: Independence from Belgium was followed immediately by secession, foreign intervention and the UN's largest peacekeeping operation to date, ending in Mobutu's seizure of power.

title: Construction of the Berlin Wall
description: East Germany erected a wall dividing East and West Berlin, becoming the most potent physical symbol of the Cold War's division of Europe.

title: Cuban Missile Crisis
description: A thirteen-day confrontation over Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba brought the United States and Soviet Union closer to nuclear war than at any other point in the Cold War.

title: Founding of the Organisation of African Unity
description: Thirty-two newly independent African states founded the OAU in Addis Ababa to coordinate decolonization and defend the inviolability of inherited colonial borders. It became the African Union in 2002.

title: Chinese Cultural Revolution
description: Mao Zedong launched a decade-long campaign against perceived enemies within the Communist Party that convulsed Chinese society, closed universities and cost hundreds of thousands to millions of lives.

title: Six-Day War
description: Israel defeated Egypt, Jordan and Syria in six days and occupied the Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights — the territorial basis of the conflict ever since.

title: Nigerian Civil War (Biafra)
description: The secession of Biafra triggered a war and blockade-induced famine that killed an estimated one to three million people, and became the first African conflict of the television age.

title: Prague Spring and Warsaw Pact invasion
description: Alexander Dubček's attempt at 'socialism with a human face' was ended by a Warsaw Pact invasion, after which the Brezhnev Doctrine asserted Moscow's right to intervene in bloc states.

title: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty opens for signature
description: The NPT split the world into recognised nuclear-weapon states and everyone else, trading disarmament promises and civil nuclear access for non-proliferation commitments.

sources.dataset: Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons

title: Bangladesh Liberation War
description: East Pakistan seceded after a mass killing campaign by the Pakistani army; Indian intervention ended the war and produced the independent state of Bangladesh.

title: Nixon shock ends dollar–gold convertibility
description: The United States suspended conversion of dollars into gold, collapsing the Bretton Woods fixed-rate system and ushering in the era of floating currencies.

title: People's Republic of China takes the Chinese UN seat
description: UN Resolution 2758 transferred China's seat, including the Security Council veto, from the Republic of China to the People's Republic, isolating Taipei diplomatically.

title: Nixon visits China
description: Richard Nixon's week in China ended two decades of mutual isolation and realigned the Cold War by opening a US–China opening against the Soviet Union.

title: Chilean coup d'état
description: The military overthrew the elected government of Salvador Allende, installing Augusto Pinochet's 17-year dictatorship and a pioneering programme of market liberalisation.

title: Yom Kippur War
description: Egypt and Syria attacked Israeli-held territory on Yom Kippur. The war reset Middle Eastern diplomacy and triggered the Arab oil embargo against Israel's supporters.

title: 1973 Oil Crisis
description: An OPEC oil embargo, imposed in response to Western support for Israel in the Yom Kippur War, quadrupled oil prices and triggered a global economic shock.

title: Carnation Revolution in Portugal
description: A near-bloodless military coup ended Europe's longest dictatorship and led directly to the independence of Portugal's African colonies the following year.

title: Khmer Rouge rule in Cambodia
description: The Khmer Rouge emptied Cambodia's cities and killed an estimated 1.5 to 2 million people before a Vietnamese invasion removed them from power.

title: Independence of Portugal's African colonies
description: Mozambique, Angola, Guinea-Bissau, Cape Verde and São Tomé became independent within months of the Carnation Revolution; Angola and Mozambique slid straight into Cold War proxy civil wars.

title: Helsinki Final Act
description: Thirty-five states accepted Europe's post-war borders in exchange for human-rights commitments that dissident movements across the Eastern Bloc then used against their governments.

title: Iranian Revolution
description: Mass protests toppled the Shah of Iran, and the country was reconstituted as an Islamic Republic under Ayatollah Khomeini — reshaping Middle Eastern geopolitics for decades.

title: Camp David Accords and Egypt–Israel peace treaty
description: Egypt became the first Arab state to recognise Israel, regaining the Sinai in exchange — and was suspended from the Arab League for a decade as a result.

title: Deng Xiaoping launches Chinese economic reform
description: The Third Plenum turned China towards market mechanisms and foreign investment, beginning the fastest large-scale reduction in poverty in recorded history.

title: Sino-Vietnamese War
description: China invaded northern Vietnam in response to Vietnam's removal of the Khmer Rouge, in a brief and costly war between two communist states.

title: Soviet–Afghan War
description: The Soviet Union invaded Afghanistan to support its communist government; a decade-long insurgency, backed by the US and others, ended in Soviet withdrawal.

title: Zimbabwe becomes independent
description: After a long bush war and the Lancaster House Agreement, Rhodesia became Zimbabwe under Robert Mugabe, ending white minority rule.

title: Founding of Solidarity in Poland
description: The Gdańsk Agreement legalised Solidarity, the Eastern Bloc's first independent trade union, which survived martial law to negotiate communism's end in 1989.

title: Iran–Iraq War
description: Iraq's invasion of Iran began an eight-year war of attrition with chemical weapons and roughly a million casualties, ending with no change to the border.

title: Falklands War
description: Argentina invaded the British-held Falkland Islands and was defeated after a ten-week campaign; the loss precipitated the collapse of Argentina's military junta.

title: Gorbachev comes to power; perestroika and glasnost
description: Mikhail Gorbachev's reforms of the Soviet economy and press were intended to save the system, and instead removed the fear that had held it together.

title: INF Treaty signed
description: The United States and Soviet Union agreed to eliminate an entire class of nuclear missiles — the first arms-control treaty to cut rather than cap arsenals. The US withdrew in 2019.

title: Tiananmen Square protests and crackdown
description: Student-led pro-democracy protests in Beijing were suppressed by the Chinese military, resulting in a still-disputed number of deaths and a lasting political chill.

title: Revolutions of 1989
description: Partly free elections in Poland began a year in which communist governments fell across Eastern Europe, from Hungary and Czechoslovakia to Romania.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
description: East Germany opened its borders, and crowds tore down the Berlin Wall, becoming the defining symbol of the collapse of communism in Eastern Europe.

title: Namibia becomes independent
description: Namibia gained independence from South African administration after a UN-supervised transition, the last major decolonization in mainland Africa.

title: Gulf War
description: A US-led coalition expelled Iraqi forces from Kuwait after Iraq's invasion and annexation of its smaller neighbor.

title: German Reunification
description: East and West Germany formally reunified, ending 45 years of division after World War II.

title: Yugoslav Wars
description: A series of ethnic conflicts accompanied the breakup of Yugoslavia into independent states, marked by mass atrocities including the Srebrenica genocide.

title: Dissolution of the Warsaw Pact
description: The Warsaw Pact formally dissolved in Prague, removing the Soviet military bloc months before the USSR itself ceased to exist.

title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
description: The Soviet Union formally dissolved into fifteen independent states, ending the Cold War and fundamentally reshaping the geopolitical map of Eurasia.

title: Maastricht Treaty / founding of the European Union
description: European Community members signed the Maastricht Treaty, formally establishing the European Union and laying the groundwork for the euro.

title: Dissolution of Czechoslovakia
description: Czechoslovakia separated into the Czech Republic and Slovakia by negotiated agreement — the 'Velvet Divorce', and a rare peaceful state break-up.

title: Oslo Accords
description: Israel and the PLO recognised each other and created the Palestinian Authority, setting up an interim self-government arrangement that was never completed.

title: NAFTA enters into force
description: The North American Free Trade Agreement created a continental market of 370 million people; it was renegotiated as the USMCA in 2020.

title: Rwandan Genocide
description: Extremist Hutu militias killed an estimated 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu over roughly 100 days, one of the fastest and most intensive genocides in modern history.

title: End of apartheid; Mandela elected in South Africa
description: South Africa's first non-racial election made Nelson Mandela president and ended apartheid, after four years of negotiated transition.

title: World Trade Organization established
description: The WTO replaced the GATT with a permanent institution and binding dispute settlement, extending trade rules to services and intellectual property.

title: Dayton Agreement ends the Bosnian War
description: The Dayton accords ended three and a half years of war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, freezing the country into two ethnically defined entities under international supervision.

title: Handover of Hong Kong to China
description: Britain returned Hong Kong to Chinese sovereignty under the 'one country, two systems' formula, which guaranteed the territory's separate system for fifty years.

title: Asian financial crisis
description: The collapse of the Thai baht spread across East and Southeast Asia, forcing IMF programmes, deep recessions and the fall of Indonesia's Suharto government.

title: Kyoto Protocol adopted
description: The first treaty to set binding greenhouse-gas targets for industrialised countries. The United States never ratified it, and it was superseded by the Paris Agreement.

title: Good Friday Agreement
description: Power-sharing institutions and cross-border bodies ended three decades of conflict in Northern Ireland. Its border provisions became the central problem of Brexit.

title: India and Pakistan conduct nuclear tests
description: Within three weeks both states declared themselves nuclear powers, adding an overt nuclear dimension to the Kashmir dispute.

title: Introduction of the Euro
description: Eleven European Union member states adopted the euro as a common currency, with physical notes and coins following in 2002.

title: NATO's first post-Cold War enlargement
description: Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic joined NATO, beginning the eastward expansion that Russia has cited ever since as a core grievance.

title: Kosovo War and NATO intervention
description: NATO bombed Yugoslavia for 78 days without a UN Security Council mandate, ending Serbian control of Kosovo and setting a contested precedent for humanitarian intervention.

title: September 11 attacks
description: Al-Qaeda hijackers attacked the World Trade Center and the Pentagon, killing nearly 3,000 people and triggering the US-led "War on Terror."

title: US-led invasion of Afghanistan
description: NATO's response to the September 11 attacks removed the Taliban from power and began the longest war in US history, ending with the Taliban's return twenty years later.

title: China joins the World Trade Organization
description: Accession locked in China's integration into global manufacturing supply chains and reshaped industrial employment in the developed world.

sources.dataset: China and the World Trade Organization

title: War in Darfur
description: Rebellion in western Sudan met a government-backed militia campaign that killed hundreds of thousands and produced the ICC's first sitting-head-of-state indictment.

title: Iraq War
description: A US-led coalition invaded Iraq and toppled Saddam Hussein, followed by a prolonged insurgency and sectarian conflict with lasting regional consequences.

title: EU Eastern Enlargement
description: Ten countries, most of them formerly under Soviet influence, joined the European Union in its largest single expansion — reshaping the continent's economic and political geography.

title: Orange Revolution in Ukraine
description: Mass protests over a falsified presidential election forced a re-run, in the first of the two uprisings that pulled Ukraine towards Europe and away from Russia.

title: Kosovo declares independence
description: Kosovo declared independence from Serbia. It is recognised by around half of UN members and blocked from UN membership by Russia and China.

title: Russo-Georgian War
description: A five-day war over South Ossetia ended with Russian recognition of two breakaway Georgian regions — the first Russian use of force to redraw a post-Soviet border.

title: Global Financial Crisis
description: The collapse of Lehman Brothers triggered the worst global financial crisis since the Great Depression, leading to recessions worldwide and sweeping bank bailouts.

title: Arab Spring
description: A wave of pro-democracy protests and uprisings swept the Arab world, toppling long-standing rulers in Tunisia, Egypt, Libya, and Yemen and triggering the Syrian civil war.

title: Syrian Civil War
description: A civil war grew out of Arab Spring protests against the Assad government, drawing in regional and global powers and displacing millions of Syrians.

title: NATO intervention in Libya
description: A UN-mandated no-fly zone became an air campaign that helped topple Muammar Gaddafi, and the state collapse that followed made later interventions politically harder.

title: South Sudan becomes independent
description: After a referendum agreed in the 2005 peace deal, South Sudan seceded from Sudan to become the world's newest UN member state, and fell into civil war two years later.

title: Russian annexation of Crimea
description: Russia annexed Crimea from Ukraine following a disputed referendum, a move not recognized by most of the international community and a direct precursor to the wider Russia-Ukraine conflict.

sources.dataset: Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation

title: Islamic State declares a caliphate
description: Islamic State seized territory across Iraq and Syria and declared a caliphate, drawing a US-led coalition into a five-year campaign that ended its territorial control.

title: Iran nuclear deal (JCPOA)
description: Iran accepted limits on its nuclear programme in exchange for sanctions relief. The United States withdrew in 2018 and the agreement has since unravelled.

title: Paris Agreement on climate change
description: 196 parties agreed to limit warming to well below 2°C through nationally determined contributions — universal participation traded against binding enforcement.

title: Brexit referendum
description: The United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union, beginning a process that concluded with formal withdrawal in January 2020.

sources.dataset: 2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum

title: Colombian peace agreement with FARC
description: The government and FARC signed a revised peace deal after voters narrowly rejected the first, ending more than fifty years of civil conflict.

title: United Kingdom formally leaves the European Union
description: The UK's withdrawal from the EU took legal effect, ending 47 years of membership and reshaping UK-EU trade and diplomatic relations.

title: COVID-19 declared a global pandemic
description: The World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic; the resulting lockdowns, over 7 million recorded deaths, and economic disruption reshaped global politics and public health policy.

title: Hong Kong national security law
description: Beijing imposed a national security law on Hong Kong after a year of mass protests, effectively ending the territory's separate political space well before 2047.

title: Abraham Accords
description: The UAE and Bahrain normalised relations with Israel, followed by Morocco and Sudan — the first Arab–Israeli normalisations in a quarter century.

title: Tigray War in Ethiopia
description: Two years of war between the federal government and Tigrayan forces killed an estimated hundreds of thousands of people before the Pretoria cessation of hostilities.

title: Myanmar military coup
description: The Tatmadaw deposed the elected government and detained Aung San Suu Kyi, triggering mass protests and a nationwide armed resistance.

title: Taliban retake Afghanistan
description: The Afghan government collapsed as US forces withdrew and the Taliban entered Kabul, ending twenty years of Western-backed government.

title: Russian invasion of Ukraine
description: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, triggering Europe's largest war since World War II, mass sanctions on Russia, and a major realignment of European security policy.

title: Finland and Sweden join NATO
description: Finland and then Sweden abandoned decades of military non-alignment to join NATO in direct response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

title: Sudanese civil war
description: Fighting between the army and the Rapid Support Forces broke out in Khartoum, producing the world's largest displacement crisis.

title: Azerbaijan takes Nagorno-Karabakh
description: A one-day offensive ended three decades of Armenian control of Nagorno-Karabakh and prompted the flight of almost the entire Armenian population.

title: Israel-Hamas War
description: Hamas's attack on Israel and the ensuing war in Gaza caused mass casualties on both sides and triggered a wider regional crisis and international divisions over the conflict.

title: Fall of the Assad government in Syria
description: A rapid rebel offensive took Damascus and ended fifty-four years of Assad family rule, after thirteen years of civil war.
